# kernable

> kernable is an application kernel for event-sourced applications: one Rust process (the kernel) checks, orders, signs and stores commands and events, and your business logic runs in your own processes, in any language (TypeScript, Python and Rust SDKs). Every command and query goes through the kernel; a submit returns once every listener has processed its events, so the next read sees them.

**Status:** kernable 0.1: released and usable in production; the API may still change before 1.0, and the release notes say how.

For building on kernable with an agent, start with the guide: [kernable.AGENTS.md](https://kernable.com/docs/kernable.AGENTS.md). Everything in one file: [llms-full.txt](https://kernable.com/docs/llms-full.txt).

## Tutorials

- [Getting started](https://kernable.com/docs/tutorial/getting-started): a kernel, an aggregate, a read model and a client in TypeScript, Python or Rust; one app
- [Build a shop](https://kernable.com/docs/tutorial/shop/): a complete application in ten parts: aggregates, read models, a reactor, a second language, authorization, personal data, operation, accounts and sign-in with the kit, a business process

## Concepts

- [Architecture](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/architecture): what the kernel does and what your processes do; a command's way and a query's way
- [Event sourcing in kernable](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/event-sourcing): decide and fold, streams and the log, write and read side, rules across aggregates
- [Domains](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/domains): what a domain holds, its rules, services and apps, a code layout
- [How the pieces fit](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/pieces): aggregates, read models, reactors, middleware and processes together, on one example
- [Order and consistency](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/ordering): one command per aggregate, listener order, who counts, settling
- [Unique keys and conditions](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/uniqueness): unique keys and facts an aggregate holds, requirements by ID or by key (also absent), checked by the kernel at commit
- [Trust](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/trust): keys, grants, signatures, the hash chain, what if something is compromised
- [Compliance](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/compliance): the technical controls kernable covers for ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GoBD, the GDPR, NIS2 and DORA, and where it stops
- [Queries and middleware](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/queries-and-middleware): every read through the kernel, middleware before and after, the request context
- [Business processes](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/processes): flows across commands, events and queries, run by the kernel: cases, waits, timeouts, incidents
- [Data over time](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/data): where kernable keeps what, event versions, the vault, snapshots
- [Failures and recovery](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/failures): what happens when something fails, guarantees, finding the cause
- [Compared with other systems](https://kernable.com/docs/concepts/comparison): kernable next to event stores, event sourcing frameworks, logs and a database with an outbox
